intent.raw_query: Patagonia hiking Torres del Paine, $4500, 12 days, December 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through the heart of Torres del Paine National Park. The trail covers approximately 80km and passes through stunning landscapes including the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the iconic Torres lookout. Book refugios or campsites in advance for overnight stays along the route.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Wake before dawn and hike 4-5 hours to the iconic granite towers viewpoint. Witnessing the first light of sunrise paint the three towering peaks in shades of gold and pink is one of Patagonia's most breathtaking natural spectacles. The trail begins at Hotel Las Torres and ascends through lenga beech forest and glacial moraine.
experiences.location: Sector Las Torres, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through icy turquoise waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most spectacular ice formations. Guided kayaking tours take you up close to towering ice walls and floating icebergs while expert guides share insights about glacial formation and Patagonian ecology. A truly immersive nature experience unlike any other.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Western Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Trek
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley surrounded by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and jagged peaks including Paine Grande and Cuernos del Paine. The trail rewards trekkers with panoramic views from the Mirador Británico viewpoint and the chance to witness frequent ice avalanches crashing from the cliffs above.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Pampas Wildlife Safari & Condor Watching
experiences.description: Join a guided nature walk across the open Patagonian steppe to spot the park's incredible wildlife including guanacos, rheas, Patagonian foxes, pumas, and the majestic Andean condor soaring overhead. Expert naturalist guides provide deep ecological context about the unique Patagonian ecosystem and increase your chances of rare wildlife sightings during golden hour.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga Entrance Zone, Eastern Torres del Paine National Park

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Torres del Paine, Patagonia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives late at night
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives late at night
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange pre-booked budget transfer or shared shuttle to Puerto Natales (approx. 1.5-2 hrs). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia. Grab a light snack if available at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Meal on flight or skip
meals.lunch: Meal on flight or airport snack
meals.dinner: Light snack from convenience store or vending machine near hotel — arrive too late for restaurant dining

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a shared shuttle from the airport to reduce transfer costs. Confirm check-in arrangements with Aegean Bliss Resort for late-night arrival. Pack a few energy bars in your carry-on for this evening. Rest well — big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, enjoy a budget breakfast at the hotel or nearby café. Walk around Puerto Natales town, visit the waterfront Costanera promenade along Última Esperanza Sound, and get oriented with the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Museo Histórico Municipal de Puerto Natales to learn about Patagonian history and indigenous cultures. Head to the local market (Feria Artesanal) to pick up affordable snacks, dried fruits, nuts, and energy bars for upcoming treks. Purchase or rent any missing trekking gear at budget outdoor shops on Baquedano Street.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the waterfront at golden hour — December light lasts until nearly 11pm in Patagonia. Plan and review your trekking maps for the coming days. Attend a free or low-cost trekking orientation if your hotel offers one.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or budget café — try a marraqueta bread roll with avocado and coffee (~$3-5 USD)
meals.lunch: Local almuerzo (set lunch menu) at a Chilean comedor — typically soup, main, and drink for ~$6-8 USD
meals.dinner: Self-catered meal using groceries from the supermarket (Unimarc or Lider) — pasta, canned tuna, vegetables (~$5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Stock up on all trekking supplies today — food, sunscreen, blister plasters, and layers. Patagonia weather is extremely unpredictable; always carry waterproofs. December is peak season so book any park entry permits online in advance via CONAF website if not already done.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early shared bus or budget transfer from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine National Park (approx. 2.5 hrs, ~$10-15 USD one way). Enter the park and pay the entrance fee (~$35 USD for non-Chileans in peak season — keep receipt for multi-day access). Head to the Laguna Amarga ranger station and begin the easy 2-hour introductory walk to Laguna Amarga viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to Laguna Azul for stunning turquoise glacial lake views. This relatively flat 3-4 hour return trail is perfect for acclimatization. Look out for guanacos, ñandus (rheas), and Andean condors along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the park entrance or nearby Camping Torres budget campsite. Set up camp or check into the budget refugio bunk dorm. Prepare a hot meal on a camp stove. Watch the extraordinary Patagonian sunset over the pampas.

meals.breakfast: Oats, dried fruit, and instant coffee prepared at hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — sandwiches, nuts, energy bars, and fruit brought from Puerto Natales
meals.dinner: Self-cooked camp meal — instant noodles or freeze-dried trekking meal with hot tea (~$3-4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Shared buses to the park depart Puerto Natales early morning — confirm departure times the evening before. Wear layers as wind and temperature can change dramatically within hours. Budget refugio bunk beds cost approximately $25-40 USD per night and should be pre-booked in peak December season.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike: Wake at 04:00 and begin the iconic hike to the base of the Torres del Paine granite towers. The 4-5 hour round trip gains significant elevation through lenga beech forest and boulder fields. Reach the glacial tarn at the base just as dawn light turns the towers golden-pink — one of Patagonia's most breathtaking spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Camping Torres (approximately 2-2.5 hours down). Rest, eat, and rehydrate at camp. Take a gentle afternoon walk around the nearby river valley to spot wildlife and wildflowers without overtaxing tired legs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to camp for an early dinner and rest. Tend to any blisters or muscle soreness. Review tomorrow's trekking plan and repack your daypack. Sleep early to recover.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed energy bars and instant coffee consumed before the pre-dawn hike departure
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at the summit viewpoint — packed sandwiches, nuts, chocolate, and thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Hot camp meal — rice and lentils with spices, or a freeze-dried trekking meal (~$3-5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most iconic hike in Torres del Paine — do not skip it. Start no later than 04:30 to catch sunrise. The trail is well-marked but steep in the final 45 minutes over boulder fields. Trekking poles are strongly recommended. Carry at least 2 liters of water. Weather can change — if clouds obscure the towers at sunrise, wait 20-30 minutes as they often clear.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Camping Torres along the W Trek route toward Refugio Chileno and then Refugio Los Cuernos. This 6-7 hour section passes through beautiful lenga beech forest with dramatic views of Los Cuernos (the Horns) massif reflected in Lago Nordenskjöld.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos area in the afternoon. Set up camp at the budget campsite nearby. Explore the lakeshore and enjoy views of the dramatic sedimentary and granite peaks of Los Cuernos rising directly above the camp.
day_by_day.evening: Campfire (where permitted) or communal refugio common room for warmth. Chat with fellow trekkers from around the world — a highlight of the W Trek experience. Early sleep.

meals.breakfast: Porridge with honey and instant coffee at camp before departure
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten on the trail with views of Lago Nordenskjöld
meals.dinner: Self-cooked camp dinner — pasta with olive oil, garlic, and canned sardines (~$4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The trail between Torres and Los Cuernos is one of the most scenic sections of the W Trek. Pace yourself — the cumulative elevation and distance over several days adds up. Keep trekking poles handy for river crossings and muddy sections. Fill water bottles from clear mountain streams (treat with tablets if uncertain).

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Valle del Francés Day Trek: Begin the spectacular Valle del Francés hike from the Los Cuernos / Italiano campsite junction. Hike up through the glacially carved valley surrounded by hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and sheer rock faces. The valley is flanked by Paine Grande on one side and the Cuernos on the other.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to the Mirador Británico viewpoint (approximately 4-5 hours total ascent) for panoramic 360-degree views of the entire Paine massif, multiple glaciers, and the valley below. Descend back to the valley floor. This full day hike covers 16-20 km round trip.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Camping Italiano or Los Cuernos area. Rest weary legs. Prepare a hearty camp dinner. The long Patagonian daylight means you can enjoy views well into the evening. Journal or photograph the extraordinary scenery.

meals.breakfast: Oats, dried mango, and coffee at camp before the big day hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mirador Británico — the best lunch view you will ever have
meals.dinner: Reward meal — slightly more indulgent camp dinner: instant mashed potato with canned corned beef and hot chocolate (~$5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is widely considered the most dramatic section of the W Trek. The hanging glaciers calve frequently — listen for thunderous booms and watch for ice falling. Do not approach glacier edges. The upper section above Mirador Británico requires good weather — turn back if visibility drops significantly. Carry extra layers as the valley can be windy and cold even in December.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day at camp. Sleep later than usual. Take a gentle lakeside walk along Lago Nordenskjöld in the morning. Photograph the reflections of Los Cuernos in the still morning water. Do light stretching and look after any blisters or muscle soreness.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek the relatively easy section from Los Cuernos camp westward toward Refugio Paine Grande along the lakeshore (approximately 3-4 hours). This flatter trail offers continuous views of the lake and mountains. Arrive at Paine Grande refugio and campsite.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Paine Grande area. Watch for condors soaring on thermals above the peaks. Prepare dinner and socialize with other trekkers. Tomorrow is a big day so pack your bag and sleep early.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast — instant pancakes with honey and coffee
meals.lunch: Snack lunch on the trail — crackers with peanut butter and dried fruit
meals.dinner: Camp dinner at Paine Grande — lentil soup with bread (~$3-4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a strategic rest and repositioning day. Paine Grande is the hub for the western side of the W Trek and the launching point for the Grey Glacier hike. Confirm your campsite reservation at Paine Grande. The refugio has a small shop with basic supplies at premium prices — stock up in Puerto Natales instead.

day_by_day.morning: Hike from Paine Grande to Glacier Grey — the third arm of the W Trek. The 4-hour (one way) trail winds through wind-sculpted lenga beech forest and open moorland with increasingly dramatic views of the massive Grey Glacier and its iceberg-studded lake. Reach the glacier viewpoint for jaw-dropping close-up views of the blue ice face.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend time at the glacier viewpoint — watch icebergs calve and float across Lago Grey. Walk to the upper glacier mirador for even better views. Begin the return hike to Paine Grande (approximately 3.5-4 hours back). This is a 20-22 km day.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at Paine Grande camp tired but exhilarated. This completes the full W Trek circuit. Hot camp dinner and well-deserved rest. Celebrate completing one of South America's greatest treks with a small treat — a chocolate bar or hot toddy.

meals.breakfast: Early oats and coffee before the glacier hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at the glacier viewpoint — the ultimate picnic backdrop
meals.dinner: Celebratory camp dinner — couscous with sun-dried tomatoes, olives, and cheese (~$5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier is one of the largest glaciers in Patagonia outside of the ice fields. Its vivid blue color comes from compressed ancient ice. Do not attempt to walk on the glacier without a guided tour — the terrain is extremely dangerous. Budget glacier kayaking or trekking tours are available but add cost. The return hike is the same trail so pace yourself on the way out.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning catamaran or ferry from Paine Grande across Lago Pehoé back toward the park entrance (approximately 30-45 minutes, ~$25-30 USD — worth it to save legs after W Trek). Alternatively, hike the full trail back if budget is very tight. Transfer by bus to Puerto Natales.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Puerto Natales by early afternoon. Check back into Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a long hot shower — the best shower of your life after days of camping. Do laundry at the hotel or a local laundromat (~$5-8 USD). Rest and recover.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a proper restaurant dinner in Puerto Natales to celebrate completing the W Trek. Explore the town in the long evening light. Visit a local craft beer bar for a well-earned Patagonian cerveza.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before departing Paine Grande
meals.lunch: Hot meal at a Puerto Natales restaurant upon arrival — the first hot restaurant meal in days
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant dinner — try Asado (Chilean BBQ) or a lamb stew at a local parilla (~$12-15 USD as a treat)

day_by_day.notes: The catamaran schedule is weather dependent — high winds can cancel crossings. Have a backup plan to hike out if needed. This is a well-deserved recovery day. Check your feet for blisters, your body for any injuries, and rest properly before the final days of exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cueva del Milodón Natural Monument — a giant prehistoric cave 24 km from Puerto Natales where remains of the extinct giant ground sloth (Mylodon) were discovered. Take a local bus or shared taxi (~$5-8 USD return). Explore the cave and surrounding trails (2-3 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Puerto Natales. Visit the Museo Histórico Municipal for a deeper dive into Patagonian natural history. Browse the artisan market for affordable souvenirs — locally made wool products, wooden crafts, and dried herb bundles make great budget gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve — join the local Puerto Natales community celebrations. Many Chileans celebrate Nochebuena (Christmas Eve) with family gatherings. Some restaurants and bars will have special menus. Enjoy the festive atmosphere along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café — enjoy a slow morning
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Cueva del Milodón or a snack from the cave entrance café
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve dinner — splurge slightly on a local restaurant offering a special Nochebuena menu (~$15-20 USD) or self-cater a festive meal with wine from the supermarket

day_by_day.notes: Cueva del Milodón entrance fee is approximately $6-8 USD. The cave is impressive — a giant natural cavern with a life-size Mylodon replica. Note that Christmas Eve and Christmas Day may affect transport and restaurant availability — plan ahead and confirm opening hours.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — take a free or low-cost morning hike on the Cerro Dorotea trail directly from Puerto Natales (no transport needed). The 3-4 hour round trip hike climbs to a ridge with panoramic views of the entire Última Esperanza Sound, Puerto Natales town, and the distant Patagonian mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and spend a relaxed Christmas afternoon at the hotel. Read, journal, review photos from the trip, and reflect on the incredible landscapes experienced over the past 10 days. Take a gentle waterfront walk.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner — either a special restaurant meal or a self-catered feast at the hotel. Many hostels and budget accommodations organize communal Christmas dinners for solo travelers — a wonderful way to share the holiday with other adventurers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Festive hotel breakfast — treat yourself to a café con leche and medialunas (croissants)
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on Cerro Dorotea with panoramic Christmas Day views
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner — communal hostel meal or budget restaurant (~$10-15 USD) — look for places serving traditional Chilean cazuela or roast lamb

day_by_day.notes: Cerro Dorotea is free to hike and starts just 2 km from the town center. It is one of the best viewpoints accessible without entering the national park. Christmas Day in Chile is a public holiday — most shops and some restaurants will be closed. Stock up on food on December 24th.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Wake early for one last sunrise walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront. Pack all gear and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at the hotel if checkout is before your transfer. Do a final gear review and donate any leftover trekking food or fuel canisters to other travelers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, take a final stroll through Puerto Natales. Visit any remaining sights or shops. Purchase last-minute Patagonian souvenirs — locally produced merino wool items, artisan chocolates, and regional wines make excellent budget-friendly gifts. Head to the bus terminal or airport for your onward transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Punta Arenas airport (approximately 3 hours by bus, ~$10-15 USD) or take a direct flight if available. Depart Patagonia with extraordinary memories, thousands of photos, and legs that have carried you through one of the world's most spectacular landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a farewell café con leche and empanada at a local bakery
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Puerto Natales café before departure — try a Chilean empanada de pino (~$2-3 USD each)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or bus station snack for the journey — or pack remaining food for the road

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transfer or bus booking the evening before. Punta Arenas to Puerto Natales bus runs several times daily but books up in peak season — reserve in advance. Allow extra time for the transfer as Patagonian roads can be affected by wind and weather. Reflect on an incredible 12-day adventure — you have hiked the W Trek, seen the iconic Torres at sunrise, explored Valle del Francés, and stood before the Grey Glacier. Patagonia will call you back.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort at Torres del Paine (approximately 1.5–2.5 hour transfer depending on exact resort location). Check in, unpack, and rest. Hydrate and prepare gear for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport or convenience stop during transfer — grab sandwiches or empanadas from a petrol station deli en route

day_by_day.notes: Confirm transfer with resort in advance. Keep a light day pack accessible for overnight essentials. Set an alarm for an early start tomorrow. Currency: Chilean Pesos (CLP) — have some cash on hand.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — sleep in until 8:00. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a short orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby lakeshore to acclimatize to the altitude and Patagonian wind. Pick up any missing gear or supplies from the resort shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Torres del Paine National Park entrance (Laguna Amarga or Lago Sarmiento gate) for park registration and orientation. Take a 2–3 hour introductory nature walk along the Lago Sarmiento shoreline, spotting flamingos, guanacos, and Andean foxes in the pampas. Ideal gentle introduction to the landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Attend the resort's evening park briefing or map session if available. Lay out and organize trekking gear for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or mid-range supplement
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from resort or light snack at park entrance café — sandwiches, fruit, energy bars (~$10–15 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at resort restaurant — try a hearty lamb stew (cordero al palo) or grilled salmon, ~$25–35 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your park entrance pass if not already done online (foreigners ~$35 USD in high season). Download offline maps (Maps.me or Gaia GPS) for the park. High season December means long daylight — sunset around 10:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Pampas Wildlife Safari & Condor Watching — Join a guided nature walk (half-day, departing 8:00 AM) across the open Patagonian steppe. Spot Andean condors soaring on thermals, guanacos, rheas (ñandú), pumas (if lucky), and flamingos near lagoons. Guide explains the unique Patagonian ecosystem. Duration: ~3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the safari (~12:30), enjoy lunch at the resort. Spend the afternoon exploring the resort's surroundings — walk to the nearest mirador (lookout) for panoramic views of the Paine Massif. Rest and stretch legs for ~1–2 hours of easy walking. Prepare and pack gear for tomorrow's full-day trek.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort. Review the Valle del Francés trek route for Day 4. Optional: visit the resort lounge for a pisco sour and conversation with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before 8:00 AM departure
meals.lunch: Resort restaurant or packed lunch — empanadas, soup, and juice (~$12–18 USD)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — try quinoa salad with grilled vegetables or Patagonian trout, ~$25–30 USD

day_by_day.notes: Wear layers — Patagonian weather shifts rapidly even in summer. Bring binoculars for condor watching. Tip your wildlife guide (10–15% appreciated). Book the guided safari through the resort concierge if not pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Valle del Francés Day Trek — Depart resort by 7:00 AM via catamaran or bus to the trailhead. Begin the ascent into the Valle del Francés, a stunning glacially carved valley. Morning hike through lenga beech forest with views of hanging glaciers calving off Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine. Aim for the upper mirador by midday (~4–5 hours round trip to upper viewpoint).
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the upper Valle del Francés mirador for lunch with breathtaking 360° views of glaciers, granite spires, and the valley below. Listen for the thunderous crack of calving ice. Begin descent back through the forest, arriving at the trailhead by 3:30–4:00 PM. Catch return transfer to resort.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at resort by 5:30 PM. Hot shower, rest, and muscle recovery. Light stretching session.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast or resort breakfast at 6:30 AM
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — sandwiches, energy bars, dried fruit, chocolate, hot thermos of tea (~$0 if self-prepared)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at resort — grilled lamb chops with chimichurri and Malbec wine, ~$35–45 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Total trek distance: ~18–22 km round trip. Difficulty: Moderate-Strenuous. Bring 2.5 liters of water, trekking poles recommended, sun protection essential. Weather in the valley can change rapidly — pack a rain jacket. Start early to avoid afternoon winds.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep until 8:00. Gentle yoga or stretching on the resort deck overlooking the lake. Enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit the resort's interpretation center or read about Patagonia's geology and wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Short scenic drive or guided resort excursion to Lago Grey viewpoint (~1.5 hours). Walk the easy 2 km trail along the lakeshore to view floating icebergs calved from Grey Glacier — a stunning and accessible experience. Photography session at the blue-ice shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by 5:00 PM. Optional spa treatment or hot tub session at the resort (if available). Pack gear for the W Trek multi-day hike beginning tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — eggs, fresh bread, local cheeses, fruit, coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at resort café or nearby Lago Grey refugio café — soup and sandwich (~$15 USD)
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — pasta with Patagonian lamb ragù or vegetarian cazuela, ~$25–30 USD

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do laundry, recharge electronics, and repack your backpack for the 4-day W Trek. Confirm all W Trek bookings (refugios/campsites) through the resort concierge. Carry only essentials on the trek — resort can store luggage.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 1 — Grey Glacier Sector. Depart resort at 7:30 AM. Take the catamaran across Lago Grey to the Grey Glacier trailhead (or hike from Paine Grande). Begin trekking east along the Grey Glacier trail with jaw-dropping views of the glacier's 6 km wide face. Hike to Mirador Grey (~3 hours, 11 km).
day_by_day.afternoon: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — After reaching the glacier viewpoint, join the afternoon kayaking session (pre-booked). Paddle through icy turquoise waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier, navigating between floating icebergs. Duration: 2.5–3 hours on the water. One of the most spectacular experiences in all of Patagonia.
day_by_day.evening: Check into Refugio Grey or Camping Grey for the night. Dry gear, change into warm layers. Socialize with fellow trekkers at the refugio common room.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast at 7:00 AM before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — energy bars, nuts, dried mango, hard cheese, crackers
meals.dinner: Refugio Grey dinner service — hearty set menu (soup, main, dessert) included in refugio package, ~$30–35 USD if not included

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking must be pre-booked (Antares Patagonia or Big Foot Patagonia operators). Dry bags provided for kayaking. Wetsuit top provided — still wear thermal base layers. Refugio check-in requires booking confirmation. Trekking distance today: ~11–14 km.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 2 — Grey to Paine Grande. Wake at 6:30 AM. Breakfast at refugio. Begin the 11 km hike from Refugio Grey east toward Paine Grande, crossing open pampas and forest with views of the Paine Massif growing larger. Wind can be intense on exposed sections — lean into it!
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Paine Grande Lodge (~12:30 PM). Check in and rest briefly. Optional short afternoon hike to the Mirador Paine Grande (~1.5 hours return) for panoramic views of Lago Nordenskjöld and the Cuernos del Paine. Stunning afternoon light on the towers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Paine Grande Lodge. Hot meal and early bedtime. Legs will be tired — elevate feet and stretch hamstrings and calves.

meals.breakfast: Refugio Grey breakfast — oatmeal, toast, eggs, coffee (~included in refugio package)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on trail — peanut butter tortillas, energy gels, apple, trail mix
meals.dinner: Paine Grande Lodge restaurant — set dinner menu with soup, Patagonian lamb or pasta, dessert, ~$30–40 USD

day_by_day.notes: Total distance: ~11 km. Cumulative W Trek distance so far: ~25 km. Winds between Grey and Paine Grande can exceed 80 km/h — trekking poles are essential. Stay on marked trail at all times. Fill water bottles at refugios.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — Valle del Francés (revisited from the other side). Depart Paine Grande at 7:00 AM. Cross by catamaran to Refugio Los Cuernos side or hike around Lago Skottsberg. Begin the ascent into Valle del Francés from the western approach — a different perspective from Day 4's route. Push to the upper mirador by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Valle del Francés and continue east along the W toward Refugio Los Cuernos (~4 km from the valley junction). Arrive by 2:30–3:00 PM. Check in and rest. Short optional walk to the lakeshore for views of the iconic Cuernos (Horns) reflected in Lago Nordenskjöld.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner and rest at Refugio Los Cuernos. Share trail stories with fellow trekkers. Early sleep — tomorrow is the most iconic day of the W Trek.

meals.breakfast: Paine Grande Lodge breakfast before 7:00 AM departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at the upper Valle del Francés mirador — the most scenic picnic spot in Patagonia
meals.dinner: Refugio Los Cuernos set dinner — typically includes salad bar, hot main course, and tea/coffee

day_by_day.notes: Total distance: ~16–18 km. This is the longest day of the W Trek — pace yourself. The catamaran schedule at Paine Grande must be confirmed the night before. Charge all electronics at refugios — no charging at campsites.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 4 — Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Wake at 3:30 AM. Headlamps on, depart Refugio Los Cuernos or Las Torres base camp by 4:00 AM. Hike 4–5 hours in darkness through lenga beech forest, crossing the moraine boulder field to reach the glacial lake at the base of the Torres del Paine granite towers. Arrive just before dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Witness the legendary alpenglow — the first pink-orange light of sunrise illuminating the three granite towers (2,850 m) reflected in the turquoise glacial lake below. One of the world's great natural spectacles. Spend 45–60 minutes at the mirador. Begin descent by 8:00–8:30 AM, arriving back at Refugio Las Torres by 11:00–11:30 AM.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer from Refugio Las Torres back to Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 45 minutes by bus/van). Hot shower, celebrate completing the W Trek! Rest, recover, and reflect.

meals.breakfast: Energy bars and thermos of hot coffee/tea before predawn departure — eat a proper breakfast upon return at Refugio Las Torres (~$15 USD)
meals.lunch: Refugio Las Torres café — burger, soup, or pasta to celebrate trek completion, ~$18–22 USD
meals.dinner: Special celebratory dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — splurge slightly on a full Patagonian feast: lamb, local wine, dessert, ~$45–55 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: This is the emotional highlight of the trip — do not miss it. Dress in full winter layers for the predawn hike (it will be cold even in December). The boulder field approach to the towers is steep and requires careful footing in the dark. Total W Trek completed: ~80 km over 4 days. Incredible achievement!

day_by_day.morning: Full rest day at the resort. Sleep as long as needed. Gentle walk along the resort's beachfront or lakeshore. Soak in the scenery without a pack on your back. Visit the resort pool or hot tub if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: Short scenic drive to Salto Grande waterfall (20–30 minutes from resort) — a powerful waterfall connecting Lago Nordenskjöld and Lago Pehoe. Easy 30-minute flat walk to the viewpoint. Dramatic and accessible. Return by 4:00 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve celebration at the resort. Many Patagonian lodges host a special Christmas Eve dinner with local music, traditional foods, and festive atmosphere. Enjoy the long Patagonian summer evening with fellow guests.

meals.breakfast: Slow, indulgent resort breakfast — fresh pastries, fruit salad, eggs any style, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at resort — grilled cheese sandwich, tomato soup, fresh juice
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at resort — traditional Chilean Christmas dishes, roast lamb, pan de Pascua (Christmas cake), local wine, ~$50–60 USD per person (special occasion)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve (Nochebuena) is the main celebration in Chilean culture. The resort may have live music or a bonfire. Dress warmly for the evening outdoor activities. Confirm Christmas dinner reservation with resort in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning at Torres del Paine — wake naturally. Enjoy a festive resort breakfast. Take a peaceful solo walk along the lakeshore with coffee in hand, reflecting on the incredible week of trekking in one of the world's most beautiful places.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final nature experience — Pampas Wildlife Safari afternoon session (or self-guided drive through the park). Look for guanacos with newborn calves (chulengos are born in November–January), Andean foxes, and condors. Visit Laguna Azul if accessible — a remote, incredibly blue lake on the park's eastern side with fewer crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening at Aegean Bliss Resort. Pack bags for departure tomorrow. Exchange contact details with fellow trekkers. Enjoy a sunset walk on the resort grounds — in December, sunset is around 10:00–10:30 PM, offering a magical golden hour over the Paine Massif.

meals.breakfast: Festive Christmas breakfast at resort — champagne or fresh juice toast, special holiday spread
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in the park or at a scenic viewpoint — resort-prepared picnic basket (~$20 USD)
meals.dinner: Final dinner at resort — order your favorite dish from the week. Toast to an unforgettable Patagonian adventure, ~$30–40 USD

day_by_day.notes: Feliz Navidad! Take time today to simply be present in this extraordinary landscape. Buy any last souvenirs from the resort shop — local wool products, Patagonian chocolate, and park-themed items make great gifts. Leave no trace — pack out all waste.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Torres del Paine. Wake early, enjoy last resort breakfast. Complete packing and check out. Take a final walk to your favorite viewpoint near the resort for one last look at the Paine Massif — photograph the towers in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Aegean Bliss Resort to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas for departure (2–3 hours). Stop at a local artisan market in Puerto Natales if time allows — buy Patagonian wool crafts, local jams, or a bottle of Chilean wine to take home. Arrive at the airport for your onward flight.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Patagonia. Reflect on 12 extraordinary days — the W Trek completed, glaciers kayaked, condors spotted, and the iconic Torres witnessed at sunrise. Patagonia will call you back.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Lunch in Puerto Natales before airport transfer — try La Mesita Grande for wood-fired pizza (~$15–20 USD) or Afrigonia for creative Patagonian fusion
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before flight departure for the transfer from the park. Confirm transfer booking with resort the night before. Declare any food items at customs when returning home. Keep trekking clothes separate — they will need washing! Total hiking distance for the trip: approximately 100+ km. Extraordinary.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route through the heart of Torres del Paine National Park. The trail covers approximately 80km and passes through stunning landscapes including the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the iconic Torres lookout. Book refugios or campsites in advance for overnight stays along the route.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Wake before dawn and hike 4-5 hours to the iconic granite towers viewpoint. Witnessing the first light of sunrise paint the three towering peaks in shades of gold and pink is one of Patagonia's most breathtaking natural spectacles. The trail begins at Hotel Las Torres and ascends through lenga beech forest and glacial moraine.
experiences.location: Sector Las Torres, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through icy turquoise waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of Patagonia's most spectacular ice formations. Guided kayaking tours take you up close to towering ice walls and floating icebergs while expert guides share insights about glacial formation and Patagonian ecology. A truly immersive nature experience unlike any other.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Western Sector, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Trek
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley surrounded by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and jagged peaks including Paine Grande and Cuernos del Paine. The trail rewards trekkers with panoramic views from the Mirador Británico viewpoint and the chance to witness frequent ice avalanches crashing from the cliffs above.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Pampas Wildlife Safari & Condor Watching
experiences.description: Join a guided nature walk across the open Patagonian steppe to spot the park's incredible wildlife including guanacos, rheas, Patagonian foxes, pumas, and the majestic Andean condor soaring overhead. Expert naturalist guides provide deep ecological context about the unique Patagonian ecosystem and increase your chances of rare wildlife sightings during golden hour.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga Entrance Zone, Eastern Torres del Paine National Park

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits you at arrivals. Enjoy a scenic night drive to the resort with a personal concierge briefing you on the days ahead. Check into your Beachfront suite, unwind with a welcome nightcap of premium Chilean pisco sour and a curated cheese and charcuterie board prepared by the resort kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or pre-departure
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or pre-departure
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity: artisan charcuterie board, local cheeses, fresh sourdough, and a bottle of Carménère from the Maipo Valley — served in-suite upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private transfer with resort 48 hours prior. Request early check-in preparation so your suite is fully ready upon arrival. Keep Day 2 light to allow for rest and acclimatization. Luggage handling is fully managed by resort staff.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast in bed or on your private beachfront terrace. Take a slow, restorative morning to recover from travel. Stroll the resort grounds and Lake or shoreline edge to absorb the first stunning views of the Torres del Paine massif rising on the horizon. Meet your dedicated resort concierge for a personalized orientation session covering the 12-day itinerary, gear requirements, and park access logistics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation drive into Torres del Paine National Park with a private naturalist guide — a gentle, non-strenuous scenic loop to key viewpoints including Lago Sarmiento and Laguna Amarga entrance gate. This introductory excursion allows your body to adjust to Patagonian altitude and weather conditions while offering your first immersive wildlife sightings. Spot guanacos, Andean condors, and Chilean flamingos along the pampas. Return to resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour on the resort's panoramic terrace overlooking the lake. Enjoy a curated tasting of three premium Chilean wines paired with Patagonian lamb skewers and smoked salmon blinis. Followed by a multi-course dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: In-suite or terrace breakfast: freshly baked medialunas, Patagonian berry preserves, farm eggs cooked to order, smoked trout, fresh fruit platter, and specialty single-origin coffee or loose-leaf tea service
meals.lunch: Light resort poolside or terrace lunch: king crab bisque, artisan sourdough, avocado and quinoa salad with lemon-herb dressing
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant: 5-course tasting menu featuring Patagonian lamb rack with chimichurri, centolla (king crab) carpaccio, wild mushroom risotto, and a decadent calafate berry tart with crème fraîche — paired with sommelier-selected wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest-and-orient day. Do not over-schedule. Patagonian weather can be intense and your body needs one full day to adjust before multi-day trekking begins. Confirm gear rental or personal gear check with resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the iconic W Trek Multi-Day Hike — Day 1 of 4. Depart resort at 07:00 with a private transfer to the Laguna Amarga park entrance. Begin trekking the eastern arm of the W toward the base of Las Torres. The trail winds through lenga beech forest and open pampas with dramatic mountain views. Your private guide leads the way, offering ecological and geological insights throughout. Distance: approximately 8–10 km with 700m elevation gain to Mirador Las Torres viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the iconic granite tower base by midday — the turquoise glacial lake at the foot of the towers is one of the world's great natural spectacles. Enjoy a gourmet packed lunch prepared by the resort kitchen at the viewpoint. Descend via the same route in the afternoon, with your guide pointing out hidden flora and fauna. Return transfer to resort by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Recovery and relaxation at resort. Utilize the spa facilities — a deep-tissue massage or hydrotherapy soak is highly recommended after the day's exertion. Light pre-dinner drinks at the resort bar.

meals.breakfast: Early power breakfast at resort: steel-cut oats with Patagonian honey and seeds, scrambled eggs with smoked salmon, energy bars, and vacuum-packed trail snacks prepared by resort kitchen
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed trail lunch at Mirador Las Torres: prosciutto and aged cheese baguette, roasted vegetable frittata slice, dark chocolate, mixed nuts, fresh fruit, and a thermos of hot herbal tea
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant: pan-seared Patagonian trout with capers and lemon butter, roasted root vegetables, warm bread, and a shared calafate berry pavlova for dessert — paired with a crisp Sauvignon Blanc from Casablanca Valley

day_by_day.notes: W Trek Day 1 is the most physically demanding single day of the trek. Trekking poles are strongly recommended. Wear layered, windproof clothing. Weather at Las Torres viewpoint can shift rapidly — waterproof outer layers are essential. Confirm private guide and transfer the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 2. Pre-dawn wake-up for the exclusive Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike experience. Depart resort at 04:30 with private transfer to trailhead. Hike 4–5 hours by headlamp and first light to reach the iconic granite towers viewpoint precisely at sunrise. Witness the extraordinary alpenglow phenomenon as the first rays of Patagonian summer light ignite the three granite pillars in shades of gold, amber, and rose — one of the most breathtaking natural spectacles on earth. Your private guide provides narrative on the geology and Tehuelche indigenous history of the towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the towers and continue west along the W Trek route toward Campamento Italiano. The trail traverses open steppe and forested valley floors with continuous mountain panoramas. Arrive at the Valle del Francés trailhead by mid-afternoon for a rest and scenic picnic.
day_by_day.evening: Private transfer returns you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Champagne and strawberries await in your suite as a post-hike reward. Dinner at the resort with a focus on restorative, protein-rich cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn energy pack consumed before departure: high-protein energy bars, banana, dark chocolate, and a resort-prepared thermos of strong coffee or hot chocolate
meals.lunch: Sunrise celebration picnic at the Mirador: resort-prepared insulated lunch box with smoked duck breast wraps, manchego cheese, dried Patagonian berries, almond butter biscuits, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant: slow-braised Patagonian lamb shoulder with rosemary jus, creamy polenta, roasted beets, and a warm apple crumble with dulce de leche ice cream — paired with a bold Malbec from Mendoza

day_by_day.notes: The 04:30 departure is non-negotiable for optimal sunrise timing in December. Headlamps, trekking poles, and thermal base layers are mandatory. This is the emotional highlight of the entire trip for most guests — allow time to simply sit and absorb the moment at the viewpoint. Photography conditions at sunrise are extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 3: Valle del Francés Day Trek. Depart resort at 07:30 with private transfer to the Valle del Francés trailhead near Campamento Italiano. Begin the ascent into one of Patagonia's most dramatic glacially carved valleys. The trail climbs steeply through lenga beech forest before opening into a vast amphitheater surrounded by hanging glaciers, serrated ridgelines, and thundering ice avalanches from the Francés Glacier above. Your private guide explains the glaciological processes shaping the valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the upper mirador for panoramic views of the Cuernos del Paine, Paine Grande, and the hanging glaciers of the French Valley cirque. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch at the high viewpoint. Descend through the valley in the afternoon, with the guide leading a detailed naturalist interpretation of the endemic flora — including the striking fire bush (notro) in full summer bloom. Return transfer to resort.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset wine tasting event hosted by the resort sommelier on the lakeside terrace — a curated flight of six premium Chilean wines from Atacama to Patagonia, paired with artisan appetizers. Followed by a relaxed à la carte dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: full hot buffet plus à la carte — eggs Benedict with smoked Patagonian trout, fresh-pressed juices, seasonal fruit, and French press coffee
meals.lunch: High-altitude gourmet picnic in Valle del Francés: roasted vegetable and hummus flatbreads, cured meats, aged cheeses, energy balls, and hot soup in a thermos
meals.dinner: Resort à la carte: centolla (king crab) with garlic butter and herb oil, followed by wood-fired Patagonian lamb chops with mint salsa verde and roasted potatoes — dessert: dark chocolate fondant with raspberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is a moderately strenuous 6–8 hour day with approximately 600m elevation gain. Ice and rock fall from hanging glaciers is audible and visible — your guide will keep you at safe distances. The notro fire bush blooms brilliantly in December, making this month particularly photogenic for this valley.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 4: Grey Glacier Sector. Depart resort at 07:00 with private transfer to Lago Grey embarkation point. Board a premium catamaran cruise across the steel-blue waters of Lago Grey, drifting past enormous floating icebergs calved from the Grey Glacier. Disembark at the Grey Glacier viewpoint on the western shore for close-up views of the glacier's towering blue ice face. Your private guide explains the glacier's retreat dynamics and climate science.
day_by_day.afternoon: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — the pinnacle adventure experience of the trip. Don premium dry suits and paddle through icy turquoise waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier with expert guides. Navigate between floating ice sculptures, listen to the glacier creak and groan, and witness the raw, elemental power of one of Patagonia's most spectacular ice formations up close. This 3-hour guided kayaking experience is exclusive and limited to small groups. Return by catamaran to embarkation point and private transfer to resort.
day_by_day.evening: Private in-suite spa treatment: couples or solo 90-minute hot stone massage and aromatherapy session to recover from four days of trekking. Followed by a celebratory W Trek completion dinner at the resort's finest table.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast: avocado toast with poached eggs and chili flakes, granola with Patagonian honey yogurt, fresh orange juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: On-water picnic aboard the catamaran: smoked salmon and cream cheese bagels, fruit skewers, artisan chocolate, and hot soup — served with views of floating icebergs
meals.dinner: W Trek completion celebration dinner: 7-course chef's tasting menu with wine pairings — including centolla bisque, lamb tartare, hand-rolled pasta with truffle, Patagonian venison loin, artisan cheese course, and a signature calafate berry soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Grey Glacier kayaking requires a minimum fitness level and comfort with cold water environments. All safety equipment and dry suits are provided. Water temperature is near freezing — the dry suits are essential and non-negotiable. This is the most exclusive and memorable activity of the trip. Book well in advance as slots are extremely limited.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day after completing the W Trek sequence. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast on your private terrace with uninterrupted views of the lake and massif. Morning yoga or stretching session with the resort's in-house wellness instructor on the lakeside deck. Optional: gentle resort-area nature walk along the shoreline with binoculars for birdwatching — look for Magellanic woodpeckers, Patagonian sierra finches, and black-necked swans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a full afternoon at the resort spa: access to thermal pools, sauna, steam room, and a 60-minute deep-tissue recovery massage. Alternatively, explore the resort's curated Patagonian library lounge with a complimentary afternoon tea service. Optional short photography walk with the resort's resident photography guide to capture the golden afternoon light on the Cuernos del Paine.
day_by_day.evening: Private stargazing experience on the resort's observation deck with a resident astronomer. Patagonia's remote skies offer some of the southern hemisphere's finest star-gazing conditions — the Milky Way, Magellanic Clouds, and Southern Cross are typically visible with extraordinary clarity in December. Followed by a romantic lakeside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast: full à la carte service on private terrace — smoked trout eggs royale, fresh-baked pastries, a cheese and fruit board, freshly squeezed juices, and pour-over specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside or terrace light lunch: Patagonian lamb flatbread pizza, burrata with heirloom tomatoes and basil oil, sparkling water, and a glass of chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Lakeside candlelit dinner: whole roasted sea bass with herb crust, grilled asparagus, saffron risotto, followed by a cheese trolley selection and a warm churros dessert with dark chocolate dipping sauce — paired with a white Burgundy-style Chardonnay

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberately unscheduled recovery day. Do not pressure guests to fill every hour. The stargazing experience is weather-dependent — the resort astronomer will advise on optimal timing. December evenings in Patagonia can be surprisingly long with lingering twilight until 22:30 or later, making stargazing best after 23:00.

day_by_day.morning: Pampas Wildlife Safari and Condor Watching — morning expedition. Depart resort at 07:00 with a specialist naturalist guide for a guided nature walk across the open Patagonian steppe within the park's pampas zone. The early morning hours offer the best wildlife activity. Spot guanacos with newborn chulengos (December is peak birthing season), Darwin's rheas, Patagonian foxes, skunks, armadillos, and pumas (sightings not guaranteed but the area is prime puma territory). The guide uses radio telemetry data from park researchers to maximize wildlife encounter probability.
day_by_day.afternoon: Condor watching at a dedicated high-altitude viewpoint. Andean condors — with wingspans exceeding 3 meters — soar on thermals above the valley walls in the afternoon hours. Your guide provides detailed natural history interpretation of these extraordinary birds. Return to resort by mid-afternoon. Optional: visit to a private estancia (ranch) near the park boundary for a behind-the-scenes look at traditional Patagonian sheep farming and gaucho culture.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Patagonian asado (barbecue) experience hosted exclusively for your group at the resort's private outdoor fire pit area. A gaucho-trained chef slow-roasts an entire Patagonian lamb over open wood fire for 4–5 hours — a centuries-old tradition. Accompanied by live Andean folk music performed by a local duo.

meals.breakfast: Early trail breakfast at resort: scrambled eggs with chorizo, whole grain toast, fresh fruit, energy bars for pockets, and a resort-prepared thermos of coffee for the trail
meals.lunch: Estancia-style picnic lunch: empanadas de pino (beef and olive), sopaipillas with pebre salsa, local cheeses, and a cold Austral craft beer or sparkling water
meals.dinner: Exclusive private asado: whole-roasted Patagonian lamb with chimichurri and salsa criolla, grilled chorizo, roasted root vegetables cooked in the embers, fresh bread, and a shared dessert of dulce de leche crepes — paired with a robust Carménère and a bottle of Patagonian craft cider

day_by_day.notes: Puma sightings are possible but never guaranteed — manage expectations accordingly. December is the absolute best month for guanaco chulengo (baby) sightings as births peak in November–December. Bring binoculars and a telephoto lens if available. The asado dinner is a cultural highlight — plan to linger for 2–3 hours around the fire.

day_by_day.morning: Private fly-fishing excursion on the Rio Serrano or Lago del Toro — one of Patagonia's premier wild trout fisheries. A licensed expert fly-fishing guide accompanies you with all premium equipment provided (Sage rods, Simms waders, and a curated selection of local dry flies and nymphs). Target wild brown trout and rainbow trout in gin-clear glacial rivers framed by the Paine massif. This is a catch-and-release experience in one of the world's most pristine fishing environments.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the morning on the water, enjoy a scenic horseback riding excursion through the Patagonian steppe and lakeside trails near the resort — a 2-hour guided ride on well-trained Criollo horses with a local baqueano (horseman) guide. Experience the landscape from the perspective of the gauchos who have worked this land for generations. Return to resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef's table experience at the resort — a 6-seat intimate dinner in the resort kitchen where the executive chef personally prepares and presents each course tableside, explaining the provenance of every Patagonian ingredient. A truly exclusive culinary event.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: full hot buffet — huevos rancheros with Patagonian salsa, fresh pastries, smoked salmon platter, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee bar
meals.lunch: Riverside picnic during fly-fishing break: gourmet sandwiches on artisan sourdough, Patagonian cheese board, fruit, dark chocolate, and a thermos of hot tea or coffee
meals.dinner: Chef's table 8-course menu: amuse-bouche of smoked trout mousse on blini, centolla ceviche with tiger's milk, wild mushroom velouté, hand-rolled pasta with black truffle, Patagonian venison with juniper berry reduction, artisan cheese course, pre-dessert palate cleanser, and a signature calafate berry and dark chocolate tart — paired with a curated wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Fly-fishing licenses are arranged by the resort in advance. No prior fly-fishing experience is required — the guide provides full instruction. Horseback riding requires closed-toe shoes or boots. The chef's table must be reserved at least 3 days in advance and is subject to availability — confirm upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic helicopter flight over Torres del Paine National Park — the ultimate aerial perspective on one of the world's great wilderness landscapes. Fly over the three granite towers, the Grey Glacier, Valle del Francés, Lago Nordenskjöld, and the Cuernos del Paine from a bird's-eye vantage point. The pilot and a naturalist co-pilot provide live commentary. This 60–90 minute flight is the most exclusive experience of the entire trip and provides photographic opportunities unavailable from any ground-level vantage point.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a leisurely afternoon. Optional: guided photography walk along the lakeshore with the resort's professional photography guide — capture golden-hour light on the mountains. Alternatively, relax at the spa or in your suite. Begin preparing for the Christmas Eve celebration.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at the resort — a festive celebration with a specially curated menu, live music, and premium champagne service. The resort transforms its main dining space into an elegant Christmas setting with Patagonian botanical decorations. Midnight toast with Moët & Chandon or a premium Chilean sparkling wine.

meals.breakfast: Christmas Eve special breakfast: eggs Benedict with black truffle shavings, smoked salmon rosettes, freshly baked croissants, a champagne mimosa, and specialty single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch: king crab and avocado salad, gazpacho, artisan bread, and a glass of chilled Albariño
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala: 8-course festive tasting menu — centolla cocktail, foie gras torchon with brioche, lobster bisque, champagne sorbet intermezzo, whole-roasted Patagonian lamb loin with truffle jus, artisan cheese trolley, yule log bûche de Noël with berry compote — paired with Krug Grande Cuvée and a selection of premier cru Burgundies

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter flight is weather-dependent and may be rescheduled to Day 11 if conditions are unfavorable — Patagonian weather is notoriously unpredictable. Confirm the Christmas Eve gala dress code with the resort (smart casual to semi-formal is typically appropriate). This is a magical evening — allow the celebration to unfold naturally.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning at leisure. Wake naturally, enjoy a luxurious in-suite Christmas breakfast with champagne and a gift from the resort (typically a curated selection of local Patagonian artisan products). A gentle morning walk along the lakeshore to appreciate the extraordinary natural setting on this special day. Optional: attend a small, intimate Christmas morning gathering hosted by the resort for guests — mulled wine, carols, and a warm communal atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final full trekking experience: a private guided hike to a lesser-known, off-the-beaten-path viewpoint within the park — away from the main W Trek crowds. Your private guide leads you to a secret mirador with unobstructed 360-degree views of the entire Paine massif, the Grey Glacier, and the surrounding lakes. This exclusive route is reserved for private guided groups only and offers a deeply personal, crowd-free Patagonian wilderness experience.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Day farewell dinner — the resort's most elaborate meal of the trip. A celebratory feast honoring both the holiday and the culmination of an extraordinary 12-day Patagonian adventure. Speeches, toasts, and a personalized photo book of your trip presented by the resort concierge.

meals.breakfast: In-suite Christmas breakfast: smoked salmon and cream cheese bagels, fresh croissants with Patagonian preserves, a fruit and berry platter, a glass of Ruinart Blanc de Blancs champagne, and specialty coffee — served with a small resort gift
meals.lunch: Trail picnic at the secret mirador: roasted chicken and brie baguette, antipasto selection, dark chocolate bark with Patagonian sea salt, fresh fruit, and a thermos of mulled wine
meals.dinner: Christmas Day farewell feast: 9-course grand tasting menu — oysters with champagne mignonette, centolla bisque, hand-rolled pasta with lobster, champagne granita, Patagonian lamb Wellington with madeira jus, cheese trolley, chocolate and calafate berry bombe, petit fours — paired with a vertical of premium Chilean wines and a 1998 vintage port to close

day_by_day.notes: The secret mirador hike is a moderate 3–4 hour round trip — appropriate for all fitness levels after 10 days of conditioning. The farewell dinner is the emotional crescendo of the trip — the resort concierge will present a personalized photo book or memory keepsake. Ensure any outstanding gratuities for guides and resort staff are arranged through the concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Wake early for one last sunrise over the lake from your private terrace — a quiet, contemplative moment to absorb the beauty of this extraordinary place. Enjoy a full resort breakfast at a leisurely pace. Complete packing with assistance from resort staff. Final stroll through the resort gardens and along the shoreline. Exchange contact details with your personal concierge and guide team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-out from Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer departs for Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport. The drive itself offers final panoramic views of the Paine massif — have your camera ready for last photographs. Arrive at the airport with ample time for departure formalities. Resort concierge provides a gourmet departure hamper for the journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry with you the memories of 12 extraordinary days in one of the world's last great wildernesses — the granite towers, the glaciers, the condors, the pampas, and the raw, elemental beauty of Patagonia.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast: full à la carte service — a personal favorite from the week, ordered from the complete menu, with a farewell glass of fresh juice and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Resort-prepared departure hamper: gourmet sandwiches, artisan cheeses, Patagonian chocolates, dried berries, a bottle of premium Chilean wine, and fresh fruit — for consumption during transfer and at the airport
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination — the resort can arrange a premium airport lounge reservation in Punta Arenas or Santiago if required

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-out (12:00–13:00) from the resort to maximize your final morning without rushing. The departure hamper should be requested from the concierge on Day 11. Consider purchasing Patagonian artisan gifts from the resort boutique on your final morning — local wool textiles, calafate berry preserves, and Patagonian sea salt are excellent souvenirs. Gratuities for all guides, drivers, and resort staff should be settled before departure.
